title: GRPO · rank-1 NoRA-init
analysis: Completed 100 steps successfully. The main positive signal is faster early learning: training correctness averages 18.4% versus 12.2% in steps 1–20, and 33.8% versus 23.7% in steps 21–40. AIME25 avg@8 at step 20 is 9.2% versus 4.2% for standard rank-1 LoRA. Training correctness later levels off near 38–39%; this does not establish that NoRA causes the plateau. Final avg@8 / pass@8 is 17.9% / 36.7%, versus the reference's 20.0% / 43.3%. The trial changes initialization and alpha together (normalized A with alpha 1 versus Kaiming A with alpha 32), so the acceleration cannot be attributed to initialization alone. The next hypothesis is that periodic merge/reset may retain the faster learning while expanding the accumulated update beyond one fixed rank-one adapter. No merge/reset was used in this trial, and that hypothesis remains untested under this recipe.
